findings.title: Settra Ransomware: TTPs, Victims, and Defense Guide
findings.summary_md: MoxFive reported direct casework on Settra, a ransomware and data-extortion group first identified in June 2026 that uses double extortion and posts victims to a Tor leak site. Initial access was observed through compromised VPN credentials, followed by NetExec and Netscan for discovery, Mimikatz and Procdump for credential access, PAExec for lateral movement, and Mesh Agent for persistent command-and-control. In at least one case Settra used the STProcessMonitor_v114.sys vulnerable driver (BYOVD) to escalate privileges and disable endpoint detection, and manually cleared Windows event logs.

findings.title: Ready, Settra, Go: New Settra Ransomware Variant Deploys MeshAgent RMM
findings.summary_md: Huntress investigated two Settra ransomware incidents, one in July and one in September 2026, in which attackers deployed MeshAgent RMM for persistence, cleared Windows event logs, and disabled Windows recovery options. The July incident used a MeshAgent instance renamed to mvtcs.exe beaconing to 45.13.122.7, while the September incident used an unrenamed MeshAgent pointing to 193.5.65.114, the address Recorded Future later attributes to TAG-218 GhostFrame infrastructure. The September incident also showed BYOVD via gdrv.sys and a misspelled Windows Defender event log path that prevented log clearing.

findings.title: Settra ransomware variant deployed in recent attacks
findings.summary_md: Cybersecurity Dive reported that security researchers warned of a Settra ransomware variant deployed in recent attacks, with hackers using VPN credentials for initial access and RMM tools for persistence. Researchers from MoxFive and Huntress described the group's use of MeshAgent, a vulnerable driver to impair defenses, log clearing, and recovery tampering.

findings.title: Active Exploitation of May 2026 PAN-OS CVE-2026-0257 (Updated October 20)
findings.summary_md: Palo Alto Networks Unit 42 reported active exploitation of CVE-2026-0257, an authentication bypass in PAN-OS GlobalProtect, by ransomware operators including Qilin and Inc, with public reporting also attributing exploitation to Settra. The most significant TTP evolution was a direct pivot from the compromised VPN gateway to the virtualization layer, where attackers disabled execInstalledOnly on ESXi hypervisors and used a custom tool to perform offline credential dumping against a domain controller's virtual disk (VMDK).
